主要内容: Sears and Kmart same-store sales declined 3.9 percent in the second quarter, compared with an 11.9 percent drop in the prior period. Total revenue fell more than 25 percent, reaching $3.18 billion from $4.28 billion a year earlier. Sears attributed the decline to falling foot traffic at U.S. mall locations and ongoing store closures. The company's net loss widened to $508 million, or $4.68 per share, from $250 million, or $2.33 per share, a year ago. Sears reported the smallest decline in quarterly same-store sales in more than three years. The company also noted positive comparable sales growth of 3 percent in July and 2.5 percent in August. Sears' shares rose as much as 27 percent in after-hours trading. CEO Eddie Lampert reiterated his belief that Sears can restructure outside of bankruptcy. Sears is evaluating a bid from ESL Investments to buy parts of Sears Holdings, including the Kenmore appliance division for $400 million and the Home Improvement business for up to $80 million. A special committee is reviewing the deal. Sears also struck a deal with the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC) to release liens on certain real estate properties, paying $32 million in return. The company borrowed an additional $75 million and pledged properties as collateral. Sears faces a major debt payment next month.
